{{short description|Model in queuing theory}}
[[File:Polling system.svg|thumb|Polling server serving ''n'' queueing nodes]]
In [[queueing theory]], a discipline within the mathematical [[probability theory|theory of probability]], a '''polling system''' or '''polling model''' is a system where a single server visits a set of queues in some order.<ref name="boxma">{{Cite book | last1 = Boxma | first1 = O. J. | author-link1 = Onno Boxma| last2 = Weststrate | first2 = J. A. | chapter = Waiting Times in Polling Systems with Markovian Server Routing | doi = 10.1007/978-3-642-75079-3_8 | title = Messung, Modellierung und Bewertung von Rechensystemen und Netzen | series = Informatik-Fachberichte | volume = 218 | page = 89 | year = 1989 | isbn = 978-3-540-51713-9 | chapter-url = https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/5899 }}</ref> The model has applications in computer networks and [[telecommunications]],<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Carsten | first1 = R. | last2 = Newhall | first2 = E. | last3 = Posner | first3 = M. | doi = 10.1109/TCOM.1977.1093936 | title = A Simplified Analysis of Scan Times in an Asymmetrical Newhall Loop with Exhaustive Service | journal = [[IEEE Transactions on Communications]] | volume = 25 | issue = 9 | page = 951 | year = 1977 }}</ref> [[manufacturing]]<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Karmarkar | first1 = U. S. | title = Lot Sizes, Lead Times and In-Process Inventories | doi = 10.1287/mnsc.33.3.409 | journal = [[Management Science (journal)|Management Science]]| volume = 33 | issue = 3 | pages = 409–418 | year = 1987 | jstor = 2631860}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Zipkin | first1 = P. H. | doi = 10.1287/opre.34.1.91 | title = Models for Design and Control of Stochastic, Multi-Item Batch Production Systems | journal = [[Operations Research (journal)|Operations Research]]| volume = 34 | issue = 1 | pages = 91–104 | jstor = 170674| year = 1986 }}</ref> and [[road traffic management]]. The term polling system was coined at least as early as 1968<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Leibowitz | first1 = M. A. | title = Queues | doi = 10.1038/scientificamerican0868-96 | journal = [[Scientific American]]| volume = 219 | issue = 2 | pages = 96–103 | year = 1968 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book | last1 = Takagi | first1 = H. | chapter = Analysis and Application of Polling Models | doi = 10.1007/3-540-46506-5_18 | title = Performance Evaluation: Origins and Directions | series = [[Lecture Notes in Computer Science|LNCS]]| volume = 1769 | pages = 423–442 | year = 2000 | isbn = 978-3-540-67193-0 | hdl = 2241/530 }}</ref> and the earliest study of such a system in 1957 where a single repairman servicing machines in the British cotton industry was modelled.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Mack | first1 = C. | last2 =Murphy | first2 = T. | first3 = N. L. | last3 = Webb | year = 1957 | title = The Efficiency of N Machines Uni-Directionally Patrolled by One Operative when Walking Time and Repair Times are Constants | journal = [[Journal of the Royal Statistical Society. Series B (Methodological)]] | volume = 19 | issue = 1 | pages = 166–172 | jstor = 2984003| doi = 10.1111/j.2517-6161.1957.tb00253.x }}</ref>

Typically it is assumed that the server visits the different queues in a cyclic manner.<ref name="boxma" /> Exact results exist for waiting times, marginal queue lengths and joint queue lengths<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Resing | first1 = J. A. C. | title = Polling systems and multitype branching processes | doi = 10.1007/BF01149263 | journal = [[Queueing Systems]]| volume = 13 | issue = 4 | pages = 409–426 | year = 1993 | url = https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/5474 }}</ref> at polling epochs in certain models.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Borst | first1 = S. C. | title = Polling systems with multiple coupled servers | doi = 10.1007/BF01245325 | journal = [[Queueing Systems]]| volume = 20 | issue = 3–4 | pages = 369–393 | year = 1995 | url = http://oai.cwi.nl/oai/asset/2228/2228A.pdf}}</ref> [[Mean value analysis]] techniques can be applied to compute average quantities.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Wierman | first1 = A. | author-link1 = Adam Wierman| last2 = Winands | first2 = E. M. M. | last3 = Boxma | first3 = O. J. | author-link3 = Onno Boxma| doi = 10.1016/j.peva.2007.06.015 | title = Scheduling in polling systems | journal = [[Performance Evaluation]]| volume = 64 | issue = 9–12 | page = 1009 | year = 2007 | url = http://users.cms.caltech.edu/~adamw/papers/pollingsched.pdf}}</ref>

In a [[fluid limit]], where a very large number of small jobs arrive the individual nodes can be viewed to behave similarly to [[fluid queue]]s (with a two state process).<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Czerniak | first1 = O. | last2 = Yechiali | first2 = U. | doi = 10.1007/s11134-009-9129-6 | title = Fluid polling systems | journal = [[Queueing Systems]]| volume = 63 | issue = 1–4 | pages = 401–435 | year = 2009 | url = http://www.tau.ac.il/~uriy/Papers/article-questa-090311.pdf}}</ref>

==Model definition==

A group of ''n'' queues are served by a single server, typically in a cyclic order 1, 2, …, ''n'', 1, …. New jobs arrive at queue ''i'' according to a [[Poisson process]] of rate ''λ''<sub>''i''</sub> and are served on a [[first-come, first-served]] basis with each job having a service time denoted by an [[independent and identically distributed random variables]] ''S''<sub>''i''</sub>.

The server chooses when to progress to the next node according to one of the following criteria:<ref name="everitt">{{Cite journal | last1 = Everitt | first1 = D. | title = Simple Approximations for Token Rings | doi = 10.1109/TCOM.1986.1096599 | journal = [[IEEE Transactions on Communications]]| volume = 34 | issue = 7 | pages = 719–721 | year = 1986 }}</ref>
* exhaustive service, where a node continues to receive service until the buffer is empty.
* gated service, where the node serves all traffic that was present at the instant that the server arrived and started serving, but subsequent arrivals during this service time must wait until the next server visit.
* limited service, where a maximum fixed number of jobs can be served in each visit by the server.<ref name="takagi">{{Cite journal | last1 = Takagi | first1 = H. | doi = 10.1145/62058.62059 | title = Queuing analysis of polling models | journal = [[ACM Computing Surveys]]| volume = 20 | pages = 5–28 | year = 1988 }}</ref>
If a queueing node is empty the server immediately moves to serve the next queueing node.

The time taken to switch from serving node ''i''&nbsp;−&nbsp;1 and node ''i'' is denoted by the random variable ''d''<sub>''i''</sub>.

=== Utilization ===

Define ''ρ''<sub>''i''</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;''λ''<sub>''i''</sub>&nbsp;E(''S''<sub>''i''</sub>) and write ''ρ''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''ρ''<sub>1</sub>&nbsp;+&nbsp;''ρ''<sub>2</sub>&nbsp;+&nbsp;…&nbsp;+&nbsp;''ρ''<sub>''n''</sub>. Then ''ρ'' is the long-run fraction of time the server spends attending to customers.<ref>{{cite book | title = Analysis of Queues: Methods and Applications | first = Natarajan | last = Gautam | year = 2012 | publisher = CRC Press | isbn = 978-1-4398-0658-6}}</ref>

==Waiting time==

===Expected waiting time===

For gated service, the expected waiting time at node ''i'' is<ref name="everitt" />
:<math>\mathbb{E}(W_i) = \frac{1+\rho_i}{2} \mathbb{E}(C) + \frac{(1+\rho_i) \text{Var}(C_i)}{2 \mathbb{E}(C)}</math>
and for exhaustive service
:<math>\mathbb{E}(W_i) = \frac{1-\rho_i}{2} \mathbb{E}(C) + \frac{(1-\rho_i) \text{Var}(C_{i+1})}{2 \mathbb{E}(C)}</math>
where ''C''<sub>''i''</sub> is a random variable denoting the time between entries to node ''i'' and<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Eisenberg | first1 = M. | title = Queues with Periodic Service and Changeover Time | doi = 10.1287/opre.20.2.440 | journal = [[Operations Research (journal)|Operations Research]]| volume = 20 | issue = 2 | pages = 440–451 | jstor = 169005| year = 1972 }}</ref>
:<math>\mathbb{E}(C) = \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{\mathbb{E}(d_i)}{1-\rho}</math>
The variance of ''C''<sub>''i''</sub> is more complicated and a straightforward calculation requires solving ''n''<sup>2</sup> linear equations and ''n''<sup>2</sup> unknowns,<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Ferguson | first1 = M. | title = Computation of the Variance of the Waiting Time for Token Rings | doi = 10.1109/JSAC.1986.1146407 | journal = [[IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications]]| volume = 4 | issue = 6 | pages = 775–782 | year = 1986 }}</ref> however it is possible to compute from ''n'' equations.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Sarkar | first1 = D. | last2 = Zangwill | first2 = W. I. | doi = 10.1287/mnsc.35.12.1463 | title = Expected Waiting Time for Nonsymmetric Cyclic Queueing Systems—Exact Results and Applications | journal = [[Management Science (journal)|Management Science]]| volume = 35 | issue = 12 | page = 1463 | year = 1989 | jstor = 2632232}}</ref>

==Heavy traffic==

{{main|Heavy traffic approximation}}
The workload process can be approximated by a [[reflected Brownian motion]] in a heavily loaded and suitably scaled system if switching servers is immediate<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Coffman | first1 = E. G. | author-link1 = Edward G. Coffman, Jr.| last2 = Puhalskii | first2 = A. A. | last3 = Reiman | first3 = M. I. | doi = 10.1214/aoap/1177004701 | title = Polling Systems with Zero Switchover Times: A Heavy-Traffic Averaging Principle | journal = The Annals of Applied Probability | volume = 5 | issue = 3 | page = 681 | year = 1995 | url = http://www.ee.columbia.edu/~egc/webpapers/system.ps| jstor = 2245120| doi-access = free }}</ref> and a [[Bessel process]] when switching servers takes time.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Coffman | first1 = E. G. | author-link1 = Edward G. Coffman, Jr. | last2 = Puhalskii | first2 = A. A. | last3 = Reiman | first3 = M. I. | doi = 10.1287/moor.23.2.257 | title = Polling Systems in Heavy Traffic: A Bessel Process Limit | journal = [[Mathematics of Operations Research]] | volume = 23 | issue = 2 | pages = 257–304 | year = 1998 | jstor = 3690512 }}</ref>

==Applications==

Polling systems have been used to model [[Token Ring]] networks.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Bux | first1 = W. | title = Token-ring local-area networks and their performance | doi = 10.1109/5.18625 | journal = [[Proceedings of the IEEE]]| volume = 77 | issue = 2 | pages = 238–256 | year = 1989 }}</ref>
